sources.finding: The documented POST /orders transaction debits the organisation balance. The documented request schema has no client idempotency key or client order reference. Success returns orderReference.
GET /orders/{orderReference} needs the orderReference, so it cannot recover an accepted transaction when the POST response containing the reference was lost.
GET /orders supports date-window filtering and pagination, but matching by time, bundle, amount and currency is not a unique job correlation guarantee.
General idempotency documentation describes Idempotency-Key, replay/retry headers and a default 24-hour retention period; it directs users to the API reference to identify supported endpoints.

The new-eSIM recipe creates an account/subscriber then a subscription activation order and receives asynchronous profile-ready and order-result events. Public docs reviewed do not yet prove that the exact activation-order endpoint accepts Idempotency-Key.

implementationState.esimGoTransactionRetry: NEVER; a durable one-shot dispatch marker is stored before POST
implementationState.esimGoUnknownAcceptance: reconciliation_required; no automatic resend and no read-only recovery without a known provider order reference

contractGate: Confirm idempotency/correlation on the exact profile-issuing order operation, its account scope, retention, body mismatch behavior, concurrent request behavior, replay response, and lookup after the retention window.
Demonstrate a sandbox test where the provider accepts an order but the response is dropped; the same idempotency key must recover the same provider order/profile without a second debit.
If the exact order operation lacks durable idempotency or lookup by a persisted client reference, do not enable automatic eSIM issuance on that adapter.
notProven: provider contract, account, sandbox credentials, Japanese long-term service rights, or a live order
